paragraphs: Rav Nechemya son of Rav Yosef.
Hyman describes him as a student of Rava, as in Beitzah 28a. He said: I was standing before Rava, and I said to him, 'Is the Master doing this to sharpen it?' — and he said to me, etc.
And Hyman describes him as a colleague of Rav Papa and Rav Pappi and R-H son of Rav Yehoshua, in Moed Katan 19b, where he said: I found them sitting and saying.

And Hyman says that he was the leading authority in his town, as in Ketubot 65a: The wife of Rav Yosef son of Rava came before Rav Nechemya son of Rav Yosef. She said to him: Rule for me [a sum] for sustenance; he ruled for her. Rule for me [a sum] for wine; he ruled for her. He said: I know that the people of Mechoza drink wine. And there, 69: he sent to Rabbah bar Rav Huna Zuta of Neharda'a: when this woman comes before you, collect her tenth of the estate [for her dowry], even from the fixed mill-base.
Hyman further reports in Chullin 48a that he used to examine in lukewarm water a lung whose lobes were attached to one another (although Rava, his teacher, said that they have no examination).
And in Bekhorot 9b, that he used to redeem the firstborn donkey with boiled vegetables.
He is mentioned in Shabbat 50b, explaining the words of Rav Yosef; and in Bekhorot 11, the reading is Rav Nachman, and Hyman says it should read Nechemya.
And Hyman records in Sanhedrin 24a: Rav Dimi son of Rav Nachman [Nechemya, the reading in Dikdukei Soferim] son of Rav Yosef.

notes.text: Lachadadah means sharpening, not making a room; the named Beitzah28a passage begins the report and its immediate continuation needs a precise side check. Peshorei means lukewarm water, not an adhesion. The tenth of the estate is a daughter’s dowry share, and the itztrobala is the fixed mill-base. Hyman’s boiled-vegetable donkey-redemption claim and Nachman/Nechemya emendations remain attributed; no harmonization of the different cases is asserted.

Three whole saved William Davidson vocalized-Aramaic scalars were read and checked against raw SHA256, selectors and actual edition metadata: Ketubot65a text10 (252 characters), Ketubot69a text13 (294 characters), and Bekhorot9b text5 (272 characters). The first has the WIFE of full Rav Yosef SON OF untitled Rava coming before full Rav Nechemya SON OF full Rav Yosef; her two first-person requests FOR ME, his two grants FOR HER, and his I KNOW about the people of Mechoza drinking wine are retained, without merging the two Yosefs. The letter scalar has full Rav Nechemya son of full Rav Yosef sending TO Rabbah bar full Rav Huna Zuta OF Nehardea, WHEN THIS WOMAN COMES BEFORE YOU/COLLECT FOR HER A TENTH/EVEN FROM ITZTROBALA. Full Rav before Huna is local to this named letter and does not expand R-H in the Moed Katan colleague list. That earlier R-H remains unexpanded; its historical full Rav Huna expansion remains exact in the archived English. Hyman's leading-authority-in-his-town and student/colleague conclusions remain source claims, not new appointments, chronology or genealogy. The supplied סט remains69 without an invented amud in the body; the saved69a comparison is recorded here, not a Hebrew or print-history repair. The contextual [for her dowry] bracket and fixed mill-base lexical reading remain inherited interpretation of the tenth/itztrobala, not words newly present in Hyman. The letter scalar's additional Rav Ashi/Rav Kahana/rent statement is not imported into the notice. The Bekhorot scalar explicitly describes Rav Nechemya son of Rav Yosef redeeming with shilki AT ITS VALUE, and contrasts this with not-at-its-value. That qualification is retained as named digital context here, not inserted as Hyman's supplied words or turned into a new legal ruling. His short firstborn-donkey/boiled-vegetables report stays unchanged; shilki is an inherited lexical rendering, not an added ingredient or animal identity. The scalar's opening and closing questions and larger argument are not imported. In Chullin the revised English makes lukewarm water the examination medium rather than what attaches the lobes; the source lobes-attached-to-one-another and ALTHOUGH RAVA HIS TEACHER SAID NO EXAMINATION parenthesis retain their force. No new whole Chullin passage was read; this is a local grammatical clarification of the inherited peshorei interpretation, not medical advice or a fresh legal verification. The Beitzah sharpening question, I WAS STANDING/I SAID/MASTER/HE SAID TO ME/etc and incomplete answer remain; the older room interpretation and pending precise side check stay historical, not fresh whole Beitzah evidence. All explicit full Rav titles in the supplied heading and body are retained; Rava remains an untitled proper name and is not expanded into Rav. Papa/Pappi remain distinct. The Moed Katan I FOUND THEM SITTING AND SAYING fragment is not completed from a different text. Hyman's Bekhorot11 Nachman reading remains full Rav Nachman, while his definite SHOULD READ NECHEMYA is expressly attributed with its full force; it is not weakened to a tentative suggestion or adopted as a canonical emendation. Bekhorot11 remains unsided. In the Sanhedrin three-generation chain, Rav Dimi SON OF Rav Nachman [Nechemya, Dikdukei Soferim] SON OF Rav Yosef remains source apparatus reporting, not a new father identity or a fresh apparatus collation. All supplied locators and the Shabbat50b interpretation remain conventional except for the specific saved comparisons described above. All three original mixed notes, the current mixed note, all English histories and every root intermediate remain exact. The proposed 69a body replacement, added-value body qualification and source-resolution requests are not applied. Only this qualification is appended; BOTH p004 and p006 holds remain, with no publication, canonical source repair, note retirement or semantic/authority admission.

The whole printed notice is in volume III, p. 927. The whole Beitzah account begins at 28a and continues at 28b: Nechemya stands before Rava, who passes a knife over a basket’s rim. Asked whether he means to sharpen it or remove fat, Rava says the latter, although Nechemya perceives sharpening as his intention. Hyman quotes only part of this exchange; the omitted words and legal explanation are not inserted. Moed Katan 19b first gives Nechemya son of Yehoshua with Pappi and Papa, then an alternative report from Nechemya son of Yosef with Pappi, Papa and Huna son of Yehoshua. The alternative supports Hyman’s reported encounter without proving that the two Nechemyas are one person; the supplied R-H remains unexpanded. Ketubot 65a distinguishes Yosef son of Rava, whose wife appears, from Nechemya son of Yosef. Ketubot 69a gives the letter to Rabbah bar Rav Huna Zuta; its subsequent Rav Ashi and Rav Kahana material is not imported. Chullin 48a transmits the lukewarm-water examination in two settings, the second alongside Rava’s statement about attached lobes. These reports do not independently establish Hyman’s teacher or town-leadership conclusions. Bekhorot 9b explicitly says the boiled vegetables were worth the donkey’s value; 11a gives the corresponding report under Rav Nachman son of Rav Yosef. Sanhedrin 24a likewise has Rav Dimi son of Rav Nachman son of Rav Yosef. These readings are disclosed beside Hyman’s definite statement that Bekhorot should read Nechemya and his reported Dikdukei Soferim alternative in Sanhedrin; the exact apparatus has not been collated here. Shabbat 50b has Nechemya bar Yosef following Rav Yosef’s explanation. No title, family identity or practical ruling is newly admitted. All existing notes remain verbatim. The retained notes describe earlier review stages; their pending-source statements are preserved as that record, alongside the new comparisons above.
